h: A Jacobean giant and a garden full of veg
p: Audley End was built in the early 1600s for Thomas Howard, 1st Earl of Suffolk, and in its day it was one of the largest houses in England, built on such a grand scale that it was a palace in all but name. Much of it was later demolished to make it more manageable, but what's left is still hugely impressive, and spotting the Jacobean details is a fun game for history fans.

Don't miss the walled kitchen garden. It's a working organic garden, laid out much as it would have been in Victorian times, with vegetables, fruit trees and a long vine house. It's especially lovely in late summer, when everything is at its fullest, and it's a brilliant way to show children where food actually comes from.

Railway fans should know about the Audley End Miniature Railway, a separate attraction just across the road from the house, with little trains running through woodland. It's run independently, so it has its own tickets and opening days, but it makes a smashing add-on for families.

Saffron Walden itself is full of character. Bridge End Gardens have a hedge maze to get lost in, and up on the Common there's an old turf maze cut into the grass, a quirky bit of local history that kids love walking. Audley End railway station, a short drive away, has trains to Cambridge and London.
